key_insight: Empirical scaling laws let DC-QAOA reuse optimized parameters across weighted MaxCut graphs without target-instance variational optimization.
engineering_relevance: A small frozen coefficient table assigns circuit angles from mean degree and root-mean-square edge weight, reducing parameter-search overhead and providing initialization for local refinement.
method: Apply exact parameter covariance under uniform edge-weight rescaling.
Fit separate mean-degree power laws to offline-optimized cost and counterdiabatic angles.
Freeze the fitted coefficients to assign angles directly on new graphs.
evidence_signal: Ideal-circuit tests on 1,050 graphs across ten families and five positive weight distributions showed higher mean optimal-solution probability than fixed-angle QAOA at depths 1–4, reaching 19.36% versus 13.11% at depth 4.
watch_item: Hardware benefits were depth-dependent: on ibm_fez, 21 unit-weight 3-regular graphs showed a mean probability advantage at one layer but reversed ordering at two layers.
paper_title: Scaling Laws for Parameter Setting in Digitized Counterdiabatic QAOA
